exposure: ampicillin-tobramycin (with metronidazole for cesarean delivery) antibiotic regimen
cohort: The study included 459 maternal-neonatal dyads with singleton gestations diagnosed with clinical chorioamnionitis, who delivered after 24 0/7 weeks of gestation and were treated with one of the two specified antibiotic regimens between January 1, 2019, and December 21, 2022.
finding: Ampicillin-tobramycin, with the addition of metronidazole for cesarean delivery, was found to be a more appropriate empiric antibiotic choice for clinical chorioamnionitis due to reduced rates of early-onset neonatal sepsis compared with ceftriaxone-metronidazole.
mod_finding: The recommended ampicillin-tobramycin regimen includes the addition of metronidazole specifically for cesarean delivery.
